synopsis: HIL with data injection connects a production ECU and its real interfaces to deterministic real-time simulation, proving timing, communications, diagnostics, faults and fail-to-safe behaviour; the booklet allocates SIL to volume and HIL to timing, interfaces and faults [f533, f5283, f12057]. Injection cannot prove the sensor front end or true machine and brake behaviour when those components are bypassed or modeled, and post-intervention evidence depends on model validation [f5286, f5287, f5553]. Physical sensor stimulation tests real sensors and firmware, but has limits on targets, field of view, weather and soiling; raw-signal HIL also carries the highest relative integration effort [f4436, f4437, f8731]. A program starting in October 2026 could realistically commission one HIL bench by mid-2027, using the ISO/TS 21815-2 J1939 intervention interface, with deterministic real time prioritized over throughput [f66, f538, f8848]. About 6,000 zero-miss trials are required for a 1% miss-rate claim across 20 critical strata at 95% one-sided confidence, judged feasible only in simulation or HIL, but the required compute or HIL throughput remains unquantified [f6654, f7449]. Published on-road work provides a physical-track benchmarking precedent, but neither an off-road perception-AEB end-to-end HIL case nor an off-road OEM statement demonstrating reduced validation time was found [f10416, f535, f257].

relations.note: Both report no published off-road OEM claim of reduced validation time.
Both allocate approximately 6,000 zero-miss trials to simulation or HIL.
Both assign HIL to timing, interfaces and faults.
Both describe real ECU interfaces and production behaviour tested against real-time simulation.
Both state downstream injection cannot prove sensor front-end behaviour.
Both describe physical track tests benchmarking equivalent simulated AEB scenarios.
Both assign braking-consequence evaluation to closed-loop simulation, HIL and physical vehicle testing.
Both require mapping safety requirements to their test environments.
Stimulation limits detail why weather and soiling are mostly not reproducible.
Camera injection specifically excludes real lens flare, soiling and full HDR response.
Mining example specifies 500 ms disconnection detection and 50 ms machine response.
The standardized stop, slowdown and inhibit command path supports the recommended HIL interface.
The 23-million-Gaussian scene's 17 FPS illustrates real-time budget constraints.
Prioritizing deterministic real time explains why scene rendering performance matters.
Claimed trial-volume feasibility remains qualified by unquantified compute and HIL throughput.
Physical benchmarking provides a precedent for validating models underlying simulated braking evidence.
Sensor-specific injection engineering helps explain raw-signal HIL's highest relative integration effort.
Sensor-specific bench work depends on which sensor technologies the systems use.
